result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService, refreshOAuthTokens is called with credential.userId; when sharing is enabled it returns the raw fetch() Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. The diff then does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token = ...`, but a fetch Response has no `.data` property, so token is undefined and the assignment throws, breaking Google Calendar token refresh in the newly-added sharing mode.

judged_text: In sharing mode res is a raw fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar operation that triggers a token refresh dies with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' inside refreshAccessToken; Google Calendar is entirely non-functional in the exact mode this PR adds.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code assumes `res` has an axios/gaxios-style `.data` (`const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token`). But `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object in sharing mode (`return response;` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), which has no `.data`. This makes `token` undefined and will throw when accessing `token.access_token`, breaking token refresh (and thus Google Calendar operations) in the newly added sharing mode.
